bin/story.sh runs story commands in the caller's CWD, not the repo root --priority high --description ## What
`plugin/claude-code/bin/story.sh` resolves the repo root into `dir` (`dir=$(repo_root)`, line 223) but never `cd`s there. Every `$STORY` invocation — `story show` (232), `story list --ready` (255), `story move --if-state` (269), and the rollback move (174) — therefore runs in whatever directory the caller happened to be in.

## Why it breaks
The story CLI has no `--repo`/`-C`/`--cwd` flag, and `ensure_project` (src/storage.rs:315-323) does NOT walk up ancestors — the project root is always exactly `env::current_dir()`.

## Extent
1. `/story do <id>` invoked from ANY subdirectory of the repo fails with exit 3, 'story project not initialized in this directory; run `story init`'.
2. Worse, invoked from inside an existing dispatched worktree it does not fail — it silently reads the WRONG tracker. `.storyhook/` is version-controlled, so every git worktree carries its own independent copy. `repo_root()` correctly anchors worktree creation to the main repo (it deliberately uses `--git-common-dir`, not `--show-toplevel`), but the ready-gate and the CAS claim are then evaluated against the worktree's own `.storyhook/open/stories/`. The claim can succeed in one checkout while the worktree is created in another.

## Repro
Inside a storyhook-initialized repo, from a tmux session:
  mkdir -p src && cd src && /story do <a-ready-id>
Expected: dispatches. Actual: ok:false, 'story project not initialized in this directory'.

## Last known good
Never worked — present since the verb landed in ed4f23d (PR #42, issue #40).

## Fix
`cd` to `$dir` before any $STORY call (or run them in a subshell anchored there). Regression test: dispatch from a subdirectory.

events.title: Plugin hooks' enabled=false kill switch is inoperative for unquoted TOML

events.description:
## What

The `enabled = false` kill switch documented for the Claude Code plugin's
session hooks does not work. `read_plugin_config` in both
`plugin/claude-code/hooks/post-git.sh` and
`plugin/claude-code/hooks/stop-handoff.sh` extracts the value with:

    val=$(grep "^${key}" "$config" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.*= *"//' | sed 's/".*//' || true)

## Why it breaks

Both `sed` expressions require a literal double quote. For an *unquoted* TOML
boolean neither substitution matches, so `val` is left as the entire matched
line — `enabled = false` — which compares `!= "false"`, and the hook proceeds as
though it were enabled.

Only the non-idiomatic quoted form `enabled = "false"` actually disables the
hooks.

## Extent

- Affects `post-git.sh` (runs `story sync-git` after every git commit/merge/push)
  and `stop-handoff.sh` (runs `story handoff` on session Stop).
- The unquoted form is exactly what the plugin itself writes: the
  `story-setup` skill's own `plugin-config.toml` template emits
  `enabled = true` / `tracking = "normal"` with no quotes on the boolean.
- So a user who follows the documented instruction to disable the hooks gets no
  effect and no error.

## Repro

    printf '[plugin]\nenabled = false\n' > .storyhook/plugin-config.toml

Then trigger a git commit in a storyhook-initialized repo with the plugin
installed. Expected: post-git hook no-ops. Actual: it runs `story sync-git`
anyway.

## Related

Note a second, latent inconsistency in the same area: this repo's real
`.storyhook/plugin-config.toml` has a `[plugin]` table header, while
`story-setup`'s template writes bare keys with no header. `read_plugin_config`
is table-blind (a plain `grep "^${key}"`), so both happen to work today — but a
real TOML parser would disagree, and the two shapes should be reconciled.

## Fix

Parse the value in a way that tolerates both quoted and unquoted forms, e.g.
strip an optional surrounding quote pair after taking everything past `=` and
trimming whitespace. Add a regression test for `enabled = false`,
`enabled = "false"`, and `enabled = true`, in both the bare-key and
`[plugin]`-table shapes.

events.title: story-install skill falsely claims the CLI has no --version flag

events.description:
## What

`plugin/claude-code/skills/story-install/SKILL.md` instructs the agent to verify
a successful install with:

> Confirm it works by running `story doctor` (or `story --help` — note there is
> no `--version` flag)

The parenthetical is false. The `story` CLI does have a version flag.

## Evidence

- `src/cli.rs:136` documents it in `HELP_TEXT`:
  `-V, --version   Print the installed story version`
- `src/cli.rs:405` parses it: `"-V" | "--version" => Ok(Invocation::Version)`
- The sibling `story-update` skill already uses `story --version` correctly, so
  the two skills contradict each other.

## Extent

Documentation-only defect in one skill body; no runtime behavior is wrong. The
consequence is that an agent following `story-install` will verify with the
wrong command, and `story doctor` is a poor choice for that purpose — it exits 5
with an `AppError::Integrity` whenever the project has any data-integrity
finding, so a healthy *binary* install in a project with pre-existing integrity
issues reads as a failed install.

## Fix

Correct the parenthetical and prefer `story --version` as the post-install
verification. Sweep the other skill bodies and `references/` for the same
claim while fixing.

events.title: web_test.rs is load-sensitively flaky: wait_for_server races the server readiness handshake

events.description:
## What

`tests/web_test.rs` fails nondeterministically, swinging between 0 and 60 failures across consecutive runs on a byte-identical tree. Observed counts in one sitting: 0, 27, 57, 2, 44, 0, 0, 60, 0, 0.

Nearly every failure is a spurious `404` — e.g. `web_serve_get_story_by_id` (line 994) panicking on `Err value: StatusCode(404)`, `web_reopen_malformed_json_is_400` (line 1715) asserting `left: 404, right: 400`.

## Why it breaks

`wait_for_server` (tests/web_test.rs:3616) only polls until the TCP port accepts a connection:

    if std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr).is_ok() { return; }

But `storyhook::web::start_server` does not finish loading registry/project state until its filesystem watcher completes the `watcher_ready_rx` handshake (see `web.rs`). The listener therefore accepts connections before the server can resolve `/api/repos/<id>/...`, and any request that wins that race gets a 404 from a server that is listening but not yet ready.

`wait_for_addr` documents awareness of exactly this hazard for the *tailnet* listener, but `wait_for_server` — used by the bulk of the suite for the loopback listener — still gates on `connect()` alone.

## Extent

Load-sensitive, which is why it looks random. It correlates with `fseventsd` CPU: the readiness handshake is FSEvents-backed, so anything keeping the filesystem-events daemon busy widens the window. Reproduced with load average ~5.5.

Amplified severely on macOS by a missing `$TMPDIR/.metadata_never_index` marker (see sibling story) — with Spotlight indexing the suite fixtures, failures hit 57/123; restoring the marker dropped the same suite to 0-2.

## Repro

    for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do cargo test --test web_test 2>&1 | tail -3; done

under moderate system load. Expect at least one run with a large block of 404 failures.

## Last known good

Never reliably good; the race is inherent to the readiness probe. Surfaced during the v0.17.0 release (PR #51), which touches no Rust source.

## Fix

Gate the probe on real readiness rather than on `connect()` succeeding — poll an actual endpoint (e.g. `/api/repos/<id>/...` or a dedicated health route) until it returns non-404, with the existing 5s deadline. A test that cannot distinguish "port open" from "server ready" will keep reintroducing this class, so the preventative action is to make the ready-probe helper the only sanctioned way tests wait for a server.

events.text: [git] e35a433: chore(storyhook): track SH-51, SH-52, SH-53

Fixed in commit 4c1aed9, with a follow-on production fix in e8d4cf8 (branch rearch/w0-gate-repair, W0.1). The mechanism proven on 2026-07-28 was not the readiness race in the description but orphaned web_test processes from earlier runs holding ~100 LISTEN sockets across 19000-19095: a fresh run restarted the fixed PORT_COUNTER at 19000, collided, and because start_server's error was swallowed with .ok() and readiness was 'the port accepts a connection', the suite talked to the ORPHAN's stale registry - 78/139 failures, all spurious 404s. Three fixes, one per link: (a) start_server_with_ready reports the address the loopback listener actually got, so in-process test servers bind port 0 and are told their port - collision is impossible, not unlikely; the four tests that must know a port before the process binding it exists draw from a randomized bind-tested band outside the ephemeral range. (b) serve/try_serve_on wait for the server's own ready callback (fired after the watcher handshake) and never swallow a start-up failure; connect_sse grew a deadline, having previously retried forever against a bound-but-silent listener while holding the SSE lock. (c) DaemonGuard stops a test-launched daemon even on panic, and make test brackets the run with scripts/check-no-orphan-servers.sh, which names surviving pids from this worktree (never the installed :3456 daemon). Regression tests: serving_an_occupied_port_fails_loudly_instead_of_trusting_the_squatter (red: reported the squatter's port as ready; green: reports 'in use') and concurrent_servers_get_distinct_ports_and_serve_only_their_own_registry. THEN, with real readiness in place, ~1 run in 5 failed with 'neither became ready nor reported a failure within 10s': tailnet_identity shells out to tailscale status --json with an unbounded Command::output(), after the loopback listener is bound - and tailscaled wedges (probes found stuck for minutes, orphaned by exited servers). That is the description's original hypothesis (listener accepting before it can serve), proven, and it hits production too: story web start's daemon would sit on :3456 listening and permanently silent. e8d4cf8 bounds the probe to 3s, kills its process group on overrun and serves localhost only; regression test a_wedged_tailscale_cli_cannot_stop_the_dashboard_from_serving puts a hanging fake tailscale ahead of the real one on PATH (red: never served; green: 3.8s). web_test 143/143 across repeated runs. That production defect deserves its own story - not filed from this worktree because minting an id here would collide with ids being minted in parallel worktrees.

events.title: story new --help creates a story titled "--help" instead of printing help

events.description:
## What

`story new --help` does not print help. It creates a real story whose title is the literal string `--help`, allocating an ID and incrementing `next-id`.

## Repro

    $ story new --help
    SH-48 --help
    state: todo (OPEN)
    assignee: -
    priority: none
    type: Default

Observed directly while working on the v0.17.0 release; it burned SH-48 in a local tree and had to be manually deleted plus `next-id` reverted.

## Why it breaks

`story new <title>` takes the first positional argument as the title with no flag handling ahead of it, so any `--`-prefixed token in the title position is swallowed as content rather than parsed as a flag.

## Extent

- Any `story <verb> --help` that takes a positional is suspect; `new` is confirmed. Sweep the other positional-taking verbs (`search`, `phase create`, `member add`, `import`, `decompose`, `web register`) before closing.
- The damage is silent and persistent: it writes a story file, mutates `next-id`, and (in a storyhook-tracked repo) leaves the tree dirty. A user probing for usage gets a junk story instead of an error.
- `--help` is the conventional discovery gesture, so this is likely to be hit by exactly the users who least expect it.

## Last known good

Unknown; likely present since `story new` gained positional-title parsing.

## Fix

Handle `-h`/`--help` (and reject unknown leading `--` tokens) before positional-title parsing, for every verb that takes a positional. Preventative action: a table-driven test asserting that `<verb> --help` exits 0, prints usage, and mutates no state, run across the full verb list so the class cannot regress one verb at a time.

events.text: [git] e35a433: chore(storyhook): track SH-51, SH-52, SH-53

Fixed in commit e2531c4 (branch rearch/w0-gate-repair, W0.1). Fixed ahead of every verb parser rather than inside them: parse_invocation now recognizes -h/--help anywhere after a recognized verb and answers with that verb's help topic (aliases resolve to their canonical topic; a verb with no topic gets the general help). The sibling sweep confirmed it was never only 'new' - comment SH-1 --help recorded a comment, move SH-1 done --help archived the story, and search, phase create, member add, import, decompose and web register all read the token as data. story tui --help was worse: it launched the interactive UI, because main.rs dispatches tui before parsing happens at all; main now lets a help request fall through to the parser. Two deliberate non-changes: an unrecognized verb keeps its error (story frobnicate --help still reports the unknown command rather than papering over a typo), and story help <topic> --help stays parse_help's to answer. Verb recognition asks the dispatcher (extracted as a pure dispatch fn, called with just the verb) instead of a second copy of the verb list that could fall out of step. Preventative action as the story asked: tests/help_flag_sweep.rs is table-driven over 54 verbs and subcommand forms x --help and -h, each required to exit 0, print one of the CLI's own sanctioned help renderings (read from the binary, not restated in the test) and write nothing to stderr, followed by a byte-level comparison of the whole .storyhook tree. Red evidence: next-id changed, SH-1 archived out of open/stories, SH-2 created. Green: 3/3, tree unchanged. cargo test 49 targets green. Separate finding, not fixed here: unknown --flags in positional-taking verbs are still swallowed as data (story new --typo x creates a story titled '--typo x'). Same shape, different defect - worth its own story.

events.title: Test suite silently depends on an untracked $TMPDIR Spotlight-exclusion marker

events.description:
## What

The Rust test suite depends on `$TMPDIR/.metadata_never_index` existing on macOS. Nothing in the repo creates, checks, or documents this — the marker lives outside version control and does not survive a fresh machine or (apparently) an OS upgrade.

## Why it breaks

The suite creates many small files in `$TMPDIR` (temp git repos, storyhook fixture trees). Without the marker, Spotlight indexes them and `mds_stores` backlogs, starving the fixture-heavy web tests. The resulting slowness widens the readiness race in [[SH-51]] and the failures surface as spurious 404s rather than as anything pointing at the filesystem.

## Extent

Measured on a tree with no Rust changes:

- marker absent: `cargo test --test web_test` failed 57 of 123
- marker restored (`touch "${TMPDIR}.metadata_never_index"`): same suite, same tree, 0-2 failures across five consecutive runs

The diagnosis cost is the real damage — the symptom (404s from a live server) points nowhere near Spotlight.

## Repro

    rm "${TMPDIR}.metadata_never_index"
    cargo test --test web_test

Expect a large block of 404 failures within a few runs.

## Last known good

Unknown. The marker was present historically on this machine and was gone by 2026-07-25, plausibly wiped by the Tahoe 26.5.2 upgrade.

## Fix

Do not depend on ambient machine state. Options, best first:

1. Point the suite at its own scratch root under a directory that is never indexed (`/private/tmp` is not indexed), via a `TempDir::new_in` helper all fixtures go through.
2. Failing that, have the test harness assert the marker exists and create it, so the dependency is explicit and self-healing rather than silent.

Fixing [[SH-51]] reduces the blast radius but does not remove the dependency — the suite would still be slow, just less wrong.

events.text: [git] e35a433: chore(storyhook): track SH-51, SH-52, SH-53

Fixed in commit 2316ddf (branch rearch/w0-gate-repair, W0.1). Root cause removed rather than documented: web_test.rs no longer creates fixtures under $TMPDIR at all. scratch_root() resolves to /private/tmp on macOS (never Spotlight-indexed) and to the OS temp dir elsewhere; scratch_dir() is now the only way this suite creates a temp directory and all 134 tempdir() call sites go through it. ensure_tmpdir_is_spotlight_exempt() additionally creates $TMPDIR/.metadata_never_index when missing, so the suites still building fixtures there are protected too (they move onto the shared helper when the test-support crate lands in W0.2). Regression test scratch_dirs_live_outside_the_spotlight_indexed_tmpdir asserts fixture paths never start with std::env::temp_dir() and that the marker exists on macOS: red against a passthrough helper (got /var/folders/.../T/.tmpddEaaq), green after. web_test 140/140 in 3.25s. Deliberately minimal so it moves into the test-support crate unchanged.

events.title: StoryEvent has no forward-compat gate: a new event variant makes older readers fail the whole repo

events.description:
## What

`StoryEvent` (`src/domain.rs:179-181`) is an internally-tagged serde enum with no
unknown-variant tolerance. Adding any new event variant is therefore a **silent
breaking change to the on-disk format**: every reader built before the variant
existed fails hard, and it fails for the *whole repo*, not just the story that
carries the new event.

This is not hypothetical — it took the web dashboard down for StoryHook's own
repo on 2026-07-25.

## Why it breaks

`read_story_events()` (`src/storage.rs:721-733`) deserializes each JSONL line with
`serde_json::from_str` and propagates the first error with `?`. An unknown `kind`
tag aborts the read of that story; callers that walk every story (report building,
`story list`, the dashboard's `build_report_data`) abort the entire traversal.

There is no `#[serde(other)]` fallback, no catch-all variant, and no schema-version
field in the log that would let an old reader detect "this repo is newer than me"
and say so.

## Extent

`StoryDescriptionSet` landed in c25be1d (2026-07-23, shipped in v0.17.0). Eight
stories — [[SH-46]] through [[SH-53]] — now carry that event.

The long-lived dashboard daemon had been running since 2026-07-24 00:07 on a
pre-c25be1d build. Result: `GET /api/repos` reported

    storyhook | available: false
      unknown variant `StoryDescriptionSet`, expected one of `StoryCreated`,
      `StoryCommentAdded`, ... `StoryDeleted` at line 1 column 29

and the dashboard rendered StoryHook as a dimmed, dashed "(unavailable)" card
(`src/web_dashboard.html:2109`). Every other registered repo loaded fine — they
had no `StoryDescriptionSet` events yet.

`build_repos_json` (`src/web.rs:363-388`) did its job: it isolated the failure to
one card rather than failing the whole request. The defect is upstream of that.

Blast radius beyond this incident:

- Any long-running `story web --serve` outlives a version bump — the daemon does
  not reload its binary.
- Any collaborator or CI runner on an older build sees the repo as broken.
- Rollback to a previous release makes previously-readable repos unreadable.

## Repro

1. Check out a commit before c25be1d and `cargo build --release`.
2. Point that binary at a repo containing a `StoryDescriptionSet` event:

       ./target/release/story list

Expect a hard failure naming the unknown variant, with no stories listed —
including the ones that contain no new events at all.

## Last known good

Every release before v0.17.0 could read every log written by every earlier
release, because no variant had been added since the format stabilized. c25be1d
is the first variant addition to expose the gap; the gap itself has existed since
the enum was introduced.

## Fix

The tension: silently ignoring unknown events renders *wrong* state (a story
showing a stale description as though it were current), which is worse than
rendering none. So a bare `#[serde(other)]` catch-all is the wrong fix.

Options, best first:

1. **Schema version in the log + explicit refusal.** Record the writer's format
   version (per-repo or per-story-header). A reader that finds a version it does
   not understand fails with "this repo was written by story >= X, upgrade to
   read it" — actionable, honest, and it names the real problem instead of
   leaking a serde error to the UI.
2. **Per-story quarantine.** Have `read_story_events` collect unreadable stories
   instead of aborting the traversal, so one future-versioned story degrades to
   an explicit "unreadable" row and the rest of the repo still loads. Complements
   option 1 rather than replacing it.
3. **Unknown-variant capture with a poisoned-snapshot flag.** Deserialize unknown
   events into a catch-all that marks the folded snapshot "incomplete", so state
   is never presented as authoritative when events were skipped. More work, and
   only worth it if partial reads turn out to be genuinely useful.

Whatever ships needs a regression test that pins the compatibility contract:
a fixture log containing an unknown `kind` must produce the chosen behavior,
not a raw serde error.

## Preventative action

The defect class is "on-disk format changed without a compatibility gate." A
variant addition currently looks like an ordinary feature commit. Consider a test
that asserts the set of known `kind` tags against a checked-in golden list, so
adding a variant forces a deliberate update and a compatibility decision.

## Related

Operationally adjacent, not the same defect: the dashboard daemon does not
restart itself on upgrade, which is what let a stale reader persist for 42 hours.
Worth its own story if it recurs.

events.title: post-merge hook reads only commit subjects, so body-trailer "Closes SH-NN" never auto-closes

events.description:
## What

The managed `post-merge` hook auto-closes stories referenced by
`closes|fixes|resolves SH-NN`, but it only reads commit **subject lines**. Any
such reference written conventionally — in the commit body, as a trailer — is
invisible to it, so the story is never closed.

## Where

`src/hooks.rs`, `POST_MERGE_HOOK`:

    git log --format='%s' "$ORIG_HEAD..HEAD" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r msg; do
      echo "$msg" | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+' | ...

`%s` is the subject alone. `%B` is the raw body including the subject.

## Why it breaks

Conventional Commits — which `CLAUDE.md` mandates for this repo — put the
closing reference in a trailer, not the summary line. The subject is reserved
for a concise description under 72 characters. So the hook's trigger and the
project's own commit style are mutually exclusive in practice: following the
style guide guarantees the hook does nothing.

## Extent

Reproduced on the merge of PR #54 (merge commit 84b64e1), whose branch commit
carried a `Closes SH-55` trailer:

    $ git log --format='%s' ORIG_HEAD..HEAD | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+'
    (no output — nothing closed)

    $ git log --format='%B' ORIG_HEAD..HEAD | grep -oiE '(closes?|fixes?|resolves?)\s+[A-Z]+-[0-9]+'
    Closes SH-55

SH-55 remained `todo` after the merge and had to be closed by hand.

Corroborating history: `0aa0094`/`d08af8e` include a commit titled
`chore(storyhook): close SH-45 as done` — a manual close. The feature has
plausibly never worked for a body-trailer reference, and the workaround
(closing by hand in a follow-up commit) has become the de-facto process.

## Repro

1. `story hooks install`
2. On a branch, commit with the reference in the body:

       git commit -m "fix(x): something" -m "Closes SH-N"

3. Merge to main.

Expect SH-N to still be OPEN.

## Last known good

None known. The `%s` format is present in the hook's original definition, so
this likely never worked for body trailers.

## Fix

Change `--format='%s'` to `--format='%B'` in `POST_MERGE_HOOK`.

Note `%B` emits multi-line records, so the surrounding `while IFS= read -r msg`
loop no longer receives one commit per iteration. It does not need to: the
loop's only job is to feed text to `grep -oiE`, which is line-oriented and
already emits one match per line. Piping `git log --format='%B'` straight into
the existing `grep -oiE ... | while read match` is simpler and correct. Verify
that a commit mentioning two stories closes both.

## Preventative action

The defect class is "hook logic shipped as an untested string literal."

events.title: commit-sync scans only commit subjects, so body-referenced stories are never linked or transitioned

events.description:
## What

`story commit-sync` scans commits with `git log --format='%H %s'` — subject
lines only. A story referenced anywhere in a commit **body** is invisible to
it, so it gets no `[git]` comment and never auto-transitions from the default
open state to the `active` one.

This is the same defect class as SH-56, in a different code path. SH-56 covers
`POST_MERGE_HOOK` (auto-close) in `src/hooks.rs`; this is `commit-sync` itself
(comment linking + auto-transition) in `src/app.rs`. Fixing one does not fix
the other.

## Where

`src/app.rs`, `Invocation::CommitSync`:

    let output = std::process::Command::new("git")
        .args(["log", "--format=%H %s", &format!("--since={since_date}")])

`%s` is the subject alone. Everything downstream — `extract_story_ids`, the
`[git] <hash>: <subject>` comment, and the `todo -> in-progress` transition —
only ever sees that one line.

## Why it breaks

CLAUDE.md mandates Conventional Commits for this repo, whose subject line is
reserved for a concise summary under 72 characters. Story references
consequently land in the body. So, as with SH-56, following the project's own
commit style guarantees the feature does nothing.

The blast radius is wider than SH-56's, because `commit-sync` runs from the
managed `post-commit` hook on **every commit**, not just on merges.

## Extent / repro

In a scratch repo (`story init --prefix CS`, two stories, hooks not required):

    git commit -m "feat: something for CS-1"                    # subject reference
    git commit -m "feat: something else" -m "Closes CS-2"       # body trailer

    $ story commit-sync --since 1h
    scanned 3 commits, added 1 comments to 1 stories
    CS-1: todo -> in-progress (referenced in 84fae18)

CS-1 got its comment and its transition. CS-2 got neither, and stayed `todo`.

Reproduced against v0.17.0 (2026-07-26).

## Last known good

None. `--format=%H %s` is present in the original implementation, so body
references have plausibly never been linked.

## Fix

Not a one-token swap — this is where it differs from SH-56. `%B` emits
multi-line records, and the parser is line-oriented:

    for line in log_output.lines() {
        let (hash, message) = match line.split_once(' ') { ... };

With `%B`, a body line like `Closes CS-2` parses as hash=`Closes`,
message=`CS-2`, producing a `[git] Closes: CS-2` comment. That is worse than
the current miss: the short hash is the idempotency key
(`comment_prefix = format!("[git] {short_hash}:")`), so a garbage hash also
breaks the "safe to run repeatedly" guarantee.

Use a record-separated format and parse per commit rather than per line, e.g.

    --format=%H%x1f%B%x1e

splitting on `\x1e` for commits and `\x1f` for hash/message. Keep the comment
text as the subject alone (the first line of `%B`) — a comment carrying an
entire multi-paragraph body would be unreadable in `story show`.

Verify: a body reference is linked; a commit referencing two stories links
both; the same commit scanned twice still adds one comment.

## Preventative action

`commit-sync` has no test that exercises real `git log` output against a real
repo. `tests/story_sync_git.rs` exists — extend it with a case whose reference
is in the body, which pins both this bug and the parsing trap above.

## Related, but separate

`story help commit-sync` claims it "auto-transitions stories based on commit
patterns (e.g., 'closes SH-1')". There is no close-pattern handling in
`Invocation::CommitSync` at all — the only transition is
default-open -> `role = "active"`, triggered by any reference regardless of
wording. Either the docs overstate the feature or the feature is missing; worth
deciding, but it is a distinct defect from this one and is not filed here.

WHAT: Every error from the main CLI dispatch path is written to stdout via print!, not stderr. Confirmed empirically: `story move SH-41 done x --quiet >out 2>err` yields 54 bytes on stdout and 0 bytes on stderr (exit 2).

WHERE: src/main.rs lines 28, 68, and 81 all call print!("{}", output::render_error(...)). Only the TUI path (main.rs:13,17) and the web --serve path (main.rs:44,49) correctly use eprintln!.

EXTENT (why it matters):
1. Callers cannot suppress errors with 2>/dev/null. The storyhook-managed post-merge hook does exactly this: `story move $ID done ... --quiet 2>/dev/null || true`. 2. With --json, error payloads are interleaved into the stdout data stream that scripts parse as results.
3. Violates the POSIX convention that diagnostics go to stderr and results to stdout, which every piping/scripting consumer assumes.

  wc -c </tmp/out   # 54 — should be 0
  wc -c </tmp/err   # 0  — should be 54

events.title: Fixing SH-58 (body scanning) turns commit-sync's bookkeeping churn into a non-terminating loop

events.description:
## What

The post-commit hook runs 'story commit-sync --since 1h', which appends a [git] link comment to every story referenced by a new commit. That comment dirties the story's .jsonl, so recording it requires ANOTHER commit — whose message, in turn, may reference the same stories.

Today this converges after exactly one step, but only by accident. Verified on main at f8645a0:

- commit-sync scans SUBJECTS only (src/app.rs:1573, --format=%H %s).
- 21258cf 'chore(storyhook): record commit links from commit-sync' — no story ID in subject — appears NOWHERE in .storyhook/. No link, no new dirt. Loop ends.
- b60db32 'chore(storyhook): file SH-59 and SH-60, ...' — story IDs in subject — linked to both. Dirt.
- commit-sync is idempotent: a second run added 0 comments, no duplicates.

The two precedent bookkeeping commits in history (c54eef2, 74869d4) are both titled 'record commit link(s) from post-commit hook' — deliberately story-ID-free. That convention is load-bearing and undocumented.

## The problem

SH-58 asks commit-sync to scan commit BODIES as well as subjects. That is a correct fix for the bug SH-58 describes, but it removes the only thing terminating this loop:

1. Commit X references SH-N -> commit-sync links it -> SH-N.jsonl dirty.
2. Bookkeeping commit Y records that link. A useful message for Y explains WHICH stories it linked, so 'SH-N' appears in Y's body.
3. With body scanning, commit-sync links Y to SH-N too -> SH-N.jsonl dirty again.
4. Bookkeeping commit Z records THAT link, body mentions SH-N, ... ad infinitum.

A subject-only bookkeeping commit no longer saves you, because the body is now scanned. The only escape becomes writing bookkeeping commits with no story ID anywhere in the message — which makes them useless to read and is an unenforced human convention.

## Extent

Low blast radius today (one extra commit, terminates). HIGH the moment SH-58 lands. This is a latent trap in an already-filed, already-prioritized story, which is why it is filed separately rather than as a comment.

Note SH-56 (post-merge hook, body trailers) is lower risk: it matches only 'Closes|Fixes|Resolves SH-N', which bookkeeping commits would not contain. The exposure is specific to commit-sync's link comments.

## Fix options (evaluate before implementing SH-58)

1. **Skip metadata-only commits (preferred).** If a commit's diff touches nothing outside .storyhook/, it is bookkeeping by definition — do not scan it. Content-based, needs no human convention, self-enforcing, and kills the loop at the origin rather than the encounter point.
2. Trailer opt-out, e.g. 'Storyhook-Bookkeeping: true', with commit-sync skipping matching commits and the hook writing it automatically. Works, but relies on the trailer being present.
3. Suppress link comments for commits authored by the hook itself. Fragile — author identity is the user's, not the hook's.
4. Treat link comments as derived state and stop committing them. Cleanest conceptually, but they are event-sourced into the same .jsonl as real story data, so they cannot be separated without a storage change.

Option 1 is the recommendation.

## Acceptance

- An automated test proves the loop terminates WITH body scanning enabled: make a commit referencing a story, run the hook's commit-sync, commit the result, run commit-sync again, and assert the working tree is clean (no new comments).
- The termination guarantee is documented, so it is not re-broken later.
- SH-58 is not closed until this holds.

events.title: Add a make install target so local installs don't use cp

events.description:
## What

The Makefile has no `install` target, so installing a locally-built `story`
means copying the binary by hand. The obvious hand-rolled command —
`cp target/release/story ~/.local/bin/story` — is a footgun that produces a
binary macOS refuses to execute.

## Why it breaks

macOS invalidates a Mach-O's cached code-signing state when the file's contents
are rewritten **in place**. `cp` truncates and rewrites the destination, keeping
the same inode. If any live process still has that inode mapped — e.g. a
long-running `story web --serve` — every subsequent `exec` of that path dies
with SIGKILL (exit 137), even though the bytes on disk are correct and
`codesign -v` passes.

Verified on macOS 26.5.2, 2026-07-25:

    cp release/story ./story          # inode 549887163
    ./story web --serve &             # holds it mapped
    cp debug/story ./story            # inode 549887163 — unchanged
    ./story --version                 # exit 137

    install -m 755 debug/story ./story  # inode 549887171 — fresh
    ./story --version                   # exit 0, holder process unaffected

The failure is confusing out of proportion to its cause: the binary hashes
identically to a known-good build and passes signature verification, so nothing
about the symptom points at the copy mechanism.

## Extent

Hit on 2026-07-25 while diagnosing [[SH-54]]: `~/.local/bin/story` returned 137
for every subcommand while `target/release/story` — byte-identical, same
SHA-256 — ran fine.

`install.sh:54` already does the right thing (`install -m 755`). Only the
hand-copy path is affected, which is exactly the path a developer takes when
iterating locally.

## Fix

Add a `make install` target that builds release and installs via `install(1)`,
honouring `install.sh`'s `STORYHOOK_INSTALL_DIR` convention so both entry points
agree on where the binary goes. Comment the target with *why* it is not `cp`, so
the constraint survives future edits.

## Note

`make install` does not restart a running `story web --serve`. The daemon keeps
its old mapping and continues serving stale code until restarted — the
proximate trigger for [[SH-54]].

events.title: story state add/remove silently deletes state descriptions from states.toml

events.description:
## What
`storage::save_states` silently deletes the `description` field of every state
in `.storyhook/states.toml`. `domain::StateDef` has no `description` field, so
the value is dropped at deserialize time and never written back out.

## Where
- `src/domain.rs` — `StateDef` (slug, super, role only)
- `src/storage.rs` — `save_states` / `add_state` / `remove_state`

## Extent
Any command that rewrites states.toml destroys all state descriptions in the
file: `story state add`, `story state remove`. This repo's own
`.storyhook/states.toml` carries two descriptions (in-progress, verifying) that
would be lost on the next `story state add`.

## Repro
1. `story init` in an empty dir
2. Append to `.storyhook/states.toml`:
   [[states]]
   slug = "review"
   super = "OPEN"
   description = "Waiting on a reviewer"
3. `story state add qa --super OPEN`
4. Re-read `.storyhook/states.toml` — the `description` line is gone.

Verified against v0.16.0.

## Last known good
None — `StateDef` has never had a description field. `TypeDef` does, which is
why types.toml is unaffected and states.toml looks like an oversight.

## Blocks
SH-41 (status-configuration UI), which writes states.toml from both UIs and
would make this data loss routine rather than rare.
